subsystems.name: Tactile sensor array
subsystems.role: detects pressure, vibration and temperature across the skin surface.

subsystems.name: Event encoder
subsystems.role: converts continuous sensor signals into sparse spikes only when a change is detected.

subsystems.name: Neuromorphic processor
subsystems.role: processes spikes locally to extract features and reduce data sent to the central controller.

subsystems.name: Flexible substrate and encapsulation
subsystems.role: supports and protects sensors and electronics while allowing bending and stretching.

subsystems.name: Communication interface
subsystems.role: transmits event data to the robot's main computer with low latency and low power.

subsystems.name: Power delivery
subsystems.role: supplies low-voltage power to the skin's sensors and processors.

buildSteps.title: Design the sensor layout and neuromorphic architecture
buildSteps.detail: Choose sensor type and density, and design the spiking network that will process events.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the flexible substrate
buildSteps.detail: Deposit and pattern conductive and sensing layers on a polymer film using photolithography or printing.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the sensor array
buildSteps.detail: Place or print tactile sensing elements and connect them to the wiring.

buildSteps.title: Integrate neuromorphic chips
buildSteps.detail: Bond low-power spiking processor chips to the flexible interconnect using flip-chip or wire bonding.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate the skin
buildSteps.detail: Apply protective elastomer layers to seal against moisture and mechanical wear.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and train
buildSteps.detail: Use spiking neural network training to map sensor events to useful tactile features.

buildSteps.title: Test on a robotic hand
buildSteps.detail: Integrate the skin onto a robotic gripper or hand and evaluate dexterity and haptic feedback.

buildSteps.title: Scale up manufacturing
buildSteps.detail: Develop roll-to-roll or panel-level processes for larger areas and lower cost.

prerequisites.why: commercial flexible circuits and displays already use similar processes.
research chips exist but are not yet mass-produced for embedded use.
training methods are still an active research area.
commercial touch sensors exist, but high-resolution, flexible arrays are not yet standard.
humanoid robots are being developed but full-body sensory skins are still experimental.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes on robotic fingertips and prosthetics
pathway.unlocks: proof of concept for low-latency haptics.

pathway.milestone: pilot integration in humanoid hands for teleoperation and prosthetics
pathway.unlocks: reliable dexterous manipulation with sensory feedback.

pathway.milestone: commercial production for advanced prosthetics and collaborative robots

pathway.unlocks: safe physical interaction in human environments.
